items.headline: The EU adopted sanctions on 1,569 people and companies in Russia's military-industrial complex, its largest single package of listings
items.summary: The Foreign Affairs Council listed 826 Russian companies and 743 of their chief executives, more than half of them on the production chain for ballistic missiles, under an asset freeze and travel ban; the measures cover suppliers of semiconductors, microcircuits, radar, navigation equipment and explosives, and bring total listings under the Ukraine regime to close to 4,600.
items.why: The EU is now going after component suppliers rather than whole sectors, so anyone exporting electronics or dual-use parts eastward has 826 more companies to screen against.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia extended the closure of Riyadh's King Khalid airport with no reopening date after weekend Houthi strikes killed 18
items.summary: The civil aviation authority prolonged the suspension on Monday as the Houthis claimed a third consecutive day of ballistic-missile attacks on the airport and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile over the capital; Saturday's strike alone killed 13 and wounded more than 300.
items.why: A G20 capital is unreachable by air for an open-ended period; route Saudi travel through Jeddah and expect Brent to keep a Gulf-risk premium until the airport reopens.

items.headline: Meta released Muse Wonder at $4/$20 per million tokens and kept the stronger Muse Wonder Full inside its $50 and $200 Muse Code plans
items.summary: Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and the Muse Code terminal agent, while Wonder Full ships only to Muse Code's Power Usage ($50 a month) and Maximum Usage ($200) subscribers; both have a roughly 1-million-token context and no open weights. Meta's model card puts Wonder Full at 57.5 on SWE-Marathon against 46.3 for Claude Opus 5.5, and behind it on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (57.1 vs 59.6).
items.why: Meta now sells a frontier coding model at the same price point as Opus 5.5 and locks its best version inside its own agent, so add Muse Code to any agent comparison before your next subscription renewal.

items.headline: OpenCode 2.0 moved the 212,000-star open-source coding agent onto one shared local service and broke 1.0 plugins
items.summary: The terminal, desktop and web apps now attach to a single background service, so a session begun in the terminal continues in the other clients; the release rebuilt the API, added an embeddable SDK, let subagents and shell commands run in the background, and made Code Mode (the agent writes JavaScript that calls several MCP tools in one execution) the default for MCP servers. Plugins and server integrations built for 1.0 must be updated, and upgrades are now manual via `opencode upgrade --major`.
items.why: If you run OpenCode, stay on 1.x until your plugins are ported; if you do not, Code Mode is the first mainstream agent to batch MCP calls through generated code, a pattern worth copying for tool-heavy workflows.

items.headline: The Kospi fell as much as 7.4% to 5,914, its lowest since late July, after China's CXMT said it would launch next-generation server DRAM this year
items.summary: Samsung Electronics dropped 7.7% and SK hynix 8.8% as foreign investors sold heavily on reports that ChangXin Memory Technologies would ship DDR5 server memory by year-end; the Korea Exchange triggered its first sell-side sidecar since 19 August. The index has fallen five sessions in a row from 7,003.74 on 2 October, and the Nikkei lost 2.5% with Tokyo Electron down 6.6% and SoftBank 8%.
items.why: Korea is the most concentrated public bet on the memory-chip cycle, and a credible Chinese entrant into server DRAM is the first thing in months to dent the AI-capex trade; watch Micron and the memory names, not just Nvidia.
